court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Chandrashekhar S/O Gangadhar Wankhede vs Vandana Chandrashekhar Wankhede
facts_of_case: The marriage took place on 21.7.2007. The respondent resided with the appellant only for 2 to 3 months after the marriage and since 2009, they have been residing separately. It is contended that there has been an irretrievable break down of marriage.

legal_principles.principle: Irretrievable breakdown of marriage can be considered as a ground for divorce.
legal_principles.held: Considering which, the following substantial question of law arises: whether due to voluntary leaving the matrimonial residence and not resuming cohabitation, even during the pendency of the litigation could it be said that the requirements of Section 13(1)(i-b) of the Hindu Marriage Act were satisfied.

legal_principles.principle: Voluntary leaving of the matrimonial residence and not resuming cohabitation can be considered as a ground for divorce.
legal_principles.held: Whether due to voluntary leaving the matrimonial residence and not resuming cohabitation, even during the pendency of the litigation could it be said that the requirements of Section 13(1)(i-b) of the Hindu Marriage Act were satisfied.
